item.title: Filthy water and gunge spilling onto pavement, 21st August
item.description:
Continually blocked drains in the hand car wash are causing filthy water and gunge to spill continuously across the public footpath in the High Street. Although the offending drains are on private property, the resulting overspill is negatively affecting a public pedestrian space. This issue has been reported to environmental officers for years. It is a shame, because the workers in there are otherwise hard working and very diligent. Perhaps council officers could attend the premises and offer advice about the drainage system whilst also making clear the council's expectations regarding what is, in effect, business waste polluting public property. Thank you

item.title: Algae on the pavement, 21st August
item.description:
For more than 10 months, a persistent water leak on the pavement has worsened following recent gas works, creating multiple new leak areas. Thames Water has failed to resolve the issue despite repeated calls. The standing water has grown thick green algae, making the pavement dangerously slippery, covered in trapped debris, and swarming with flies. This creates a severe health, safety, and slip hazard for pedestrians. Main Problems Long-term leak: Ongoing for over 10 months and made worse by recent gas work.Algae growth: Thick green slime covering the walkway. Safety hazard: Extremely slippery surface causing a fall risk for walkers. Pests and dirt: Flies swarming the area and debris stuck to the wet surface. No action: Thames Water has ignored multiple phone calls. What We Want Done Please send an urgent repair team to fix the water leaks under the pavement.Clean and treat the algae-covered walkway to stop slips.Clear away the debris and standing water.

Nearest address to the pin placed on the map (from OS Places API): Ankerdine Crescent, Plumstead

item.title: Close to Priory Tavern Pub, 21st August
item.description:
There is a significant amount of loose gravel on the road at this location, creating a serious skid hazard for cyclists and other road users. On 20 August 2026 at approximately 14:30, I was cycling over this section of road when my bicycle lost traction on the gravel and I fell. I sustained injuries to multiple parts of my body and attended A&E following the accident. I have since found that this appears to be an ongoing problem. A previous report made on 11 July 2026, FixMyStreet reference 9770564, specifically reported the gravel at this location and stated that two motorcyclists had already skidded and fallen and that a car had also skidded when turning onto the road. The loose gravel therefore appears to have been present for some time and has now resulted in several reported incidents, including my own injury. Please inspect the road urgently and remove or otherwise make safe the loose gravel before another accident occurs.

Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): 250, Belsize Road, South Hampstead, Greater London
Report on FixMyStreet
